utterances.text: The map was made by the military institute in Belgrade. I don't know if that's the exact name of the institution. Perhaps it's stated somewhere. I had the original of the map. It's the military publishing institute or something like that. Generally -- well, it's the military publishing institute in Belgrade. The information is as stated in the map from the military headquarters of Krajina from June 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is the demographic breakdown of the areas just discussed as indicated in the map consistent with your understanding of the demographic breakdown in 1993?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes, more or less. I didn't know the exact data, but I assume that based on what I saw, that could be so or approximately so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now let me turn your attention back to 1990 and again to those specific areas. Can you tell the Court what the approximate demographic breakdown was in Eastern Slavonia in 1990?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: According to my estimate, half of the population were Serbs and Yugoslavs, and the rest, or the other half, were Croats and others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And according to your best estimate, what was the demographic breakdown of Banija?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Banija had about 75 per cent of Croats and 30 per cent of others. More or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Kordun, what was the demographic breakdown of Kordun in 1990?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: It was probably about 80 per cent of Serbs and the rest were others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me refer you back quickly to your previous answer. According to the transcript it indicated that Banija had about 75 per cent of Croats and 30 per cent of others, more or less. First of all, I wanted to know if that's -- the demography is correct, and second if you could reconcile the addition.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: No. No. I think the interpretation was not good. I said 75 per cent Serbs, 30 per cent others. Perhaps I made a mistake previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that still leaves the 105 per cent as a result, but it was "about", Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: 25 per cent. I apologise. More or less. I just went by the percentage of the Serbs and then I assumed about the -- how many we would have of the rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you also indicate to us the approximate demographic breakdown of Lika in 1990?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I think there were about 80 per cent Serbs in Lika and 20 per cent were others, and the same goes for Northern Dalmatia. Approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, what --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: If there are to be any more questions of this nature in relation to demographics, my objection would be that I don't think it's particularly probative coming from somebody who is not a demographer, and I would -- I would object on that basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me ask a question to Mr. Tieger. Mr. Tieger, is the establishment of demographic figures or are you establishing what the understanding of the witness was in view of political positions he might have taken? What is it about?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the rough or relative accuracy of the demographic description provided by the witness is a matter of -- is part of the Prosecution's evidence, and clearly it's not intended with -- to have the same precision as a demographic expert might be, but we're talking about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the perception of the witness of what the ethnic or demographic figures were, what he understood them to be. Do I understand to get later a more detailed report -- because this is mainly about the situation in Croatia rather than in Bosnia and Herzegovina, do we get further -- further evidence on demographic issues?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It was not my intention to do so, Your Honour. My --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not with this witness, but later on, wasn't there a report of Ms. Tabeau to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I can't say at this moment the extent to which it addresses population changes in Croatia. However, the point of addressing this issue at this time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- is again not about the specific numbers or the precise breakdown but about a population change of such significance that a witness in this -- or a person in this witness's position would be able to recognise that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Loukas, if you would ask in general a Dutchman whether it's in the north or in the south that most of the Catholics are living, you'll get a 99.9 per cent answer that's in the south. I would give that example. I would even, without ever having done any demographic studies, I would fully guarantee that the answer is right. It's not only on the basis of demographic studies that you could tell something about demographic issues.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I appreciate that entirely, Your Honour, but it was not apparent from Mr. Tieger's questioning what the point was of this evidence, and it didn't appear immediately apparently probative on any particular issue that's before the Tribunal at this point, and I wanted to make that point so we knew where this evidence was aimed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you assist a bit more, Mr. Tieger, apart from giving a global idea on then of course the relevance of that global idea on how the demographic issues in Croatia were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It may be of assistance for the Court to know that I'm about to ask the witness what exactly accounted for that demographic change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, can you tell us, please, and tell the Court, please, what accounted for the change in the demographic character of these areas?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: In the course of 1991, there was an armed conflict in Croatia during which a large number of the population from this area, Croats, were expelled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell -- can you tell us, please, what forces were involved in this effort to expel Croats from the area?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: During the military operations, the JNA, the Territorial Defence, and units under the control of the police, including also the Krajina police forces, took part in the armed conflict, and they are responsible for the expulsion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during the course of your testimony in the Milosevic case and also in your factual basis, you were -- used a term "a parallel structure." Can you tell us, please, what the parallel structure was?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: A parallel structure is a parallel structure of power and authority in the territory of the SAO Krajina, which was formed by the service, the State Security Service of Serbia. If was a parallel structure in relation to the Krajina authorities and included members of the Serbian state security, members of the Krajina police, members of the Serbian Democratic Party. At the top of the structure, of course, was Slobodan Milosevic as head of the state security, as a controller, according to what I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, who were some of the principal figures in the parallel structure?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: These were the officials of the state security in Serbia; Jovica Stanisic, Frenki Simatovic, Captain Dragan, and so on. They were the key figures in -- at the time, as well as Milan Martic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that at the top of the parallel structure was Slobodan Milosevic. What was Jovica Stanisic's relationship to Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: He was his subordinate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also mentioned Franko Simatovic. What was his relationship to either Mr. Milosevic or Mr. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Subordinated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the relationship of Simatovic to Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: According to what I know, subordinated. When I said that Stanisic was subordinated to Milosevic, I don't know how it came out in the interpretation, but that is what I meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And apart from Mr. Milosevic, what was Mr. Stanisic's position within the authority figures of the parallel structure in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: He was the head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned Milan Martic. Did he occupy -- as a member of the parallel structure, did he also occupy formal positions of authority within the governmental structures of the Serbian authorities in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: He did have functions, posts. Formally he was part of the authority of the Krajina, but actually he was part of the parallel structures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first become aware of figures involved in the parallel structure beginning to play a role in events in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: In August 1990.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened at that time to make you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: The so-called log revolution took place. So it was a conflict between the local Serbs around Knin and the Knin police with the Croatian authorities. That was called the log revolution by the Croatian press, media. At the time when those events were taking place, I met Jovica Stanisic, who was maintaining contacts with Martic. That was when I began to find out about the parallel structure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe briefly the events surrounding the so-called log revolution and the role of Mr. Martic or Mr. Stanisic in that.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: The events were a consequence of the political conflict in Croatia between the Croatian authorities, the Croatian government, which was changing the constitution of the Republic of Croatia, and between the Serbs, the political representatives of the Serbs, SDS in particular, who opposed those constitutional changes, believing they were to the detriment of the Serbian people. The political conflict culminated in the decision of the Serbian National Council to hold a referendum on Serb autonomy in Croatia and also in the decision of the Croatian government to prevent the holding of this referendum. All the other incidents took place after this, and especially the incident related to the participation of local police in Knin and Milan Martic in these events, which was actually the distribution of weapons to the reserve police and the erecting of the barricades as well as armed opposition. That, again, was a beginning of all those events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated -- you indicated earlier that the JNA and the TO were also involved in the effort to expel the population from portions of Croatia. Who was in command or in control of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: In the operational sense, it was the General Staff of the Yugoslav People's Army in Belgrade and the headquarters of the Supreme Command in conditions of imminent threat of war and state of war, and the Presidency of Yugoslavia as the collective Supreme Commander. According to my information, in such circumstances, Slobodan Milosevic as well as the most influential political figure in Serbia who did have control and influence over the JNA in the events of autumn 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the course of your dealings with Mr. Milosevic during the period 1990 through 1991, did you have occasion to see him indicate his control over the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, on approximately how many occasions did you meet with Mr. Milosevic from -- or during the period 1990 through 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Several times. In 1990.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this question: On how many occasions overall had you met with Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Approximately 20 times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first make contact with Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I made a contact in August of 1990.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you initiate that contact on your own or were you encouraged to do so by others?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Others urged me to seek contact with Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it that encouraged you to do so?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Milan Martic, Bogoljub Popovic from the Serbian Democratic Party, and some other people from Krajina. They urged me to go and meet with Milosevic and asked for protection from him, especially at the time of the events that I just described, which were in fact political conflicts with the Croatian government and the announced referendum on Serbian autonomy, and counter-announcements by Croatian government that it would use force, if necessary, to prevent that referendum. That was under those circumstances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you able to make contact with Mr. Milosevic at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I did establish contact in Kupari, near Dubrovnik, which was where Mr. Milosevic was at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Mr. Milosevic indicate to you whether he would support Serbs in Croatia; and if so, in what manner?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: He did send me that message indirectly through Borisav Jovic. He sent Borisav Jovic, who was then the president of the Presidency of the SFRY, to go and meet with us and tell us what kinds of measures would be undertaken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us what Mr. Jovic indicated to you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Jovic said that with the assistance of the JNA, he would support any political action on our part in Croatia, that he would support any political effort of ours in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before moving on to other matters, I want to quickly identify some of the political steps taken from the time of the election to the declaration of the Republic of Serbian Krajina in December of 1991. Was the first step, Mr. Babic, that an association of municipalities of Northern Dalmatia and Lika was formed which expressed the wish of the Serbian population in the area to introduce Serbian autonomy in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: That was one of the first political events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which municipalities were included in the association of municipalities?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: That was the Association of Municipalities of Northern Dalmatia, in Lika, and later on municipalities from Banija and Kordun also joined in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the association initially include the municipalities of Knin, Benkovac, Gracac, Donji Lapac, Obrovac, and Titova Korenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On July 25, 1990, did the SDS Croatia proclaim the autonomy or declare the autonomy of the Serbian people in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: That wasn't declared by the SDS but, rather, by the Serbian Assembly held in Srb, which was held at the initiative of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was the -- was a Serbian National Council also established at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the same day, were members of the Serbian National Council elected?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as I believe you indicated earlier, you became president of the Serbian National Council.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes, at the next following session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the first meeting of the Serbian National Council, did it vote to hold a referendum to determine the vote in favour or against a declaration on autonomy?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes. The decision was adopted to hold a referendum on Serbian autonomy or, rather, to implement it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that referendum ultimately held?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct that the vote taken was overwhelmingly in favour of autonomy?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Subsequently on September 30, 1990, did the Serbian National Council declare the autonomy of the Serbian people on ethnic and historic territories on which they live and which are within the boundaries of the Republic of Croatia as a federal unit of the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes, based on the results of the referendum.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A few months later, in late December 1990, did the Association of Municipalities of Northern Dalmatia and Lika transform itself into another entity?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that entity into which it transformed the Serbian Autonomous District of Krajina, SAO Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was the Serbian Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct that the statute of SAO Krajina, among other things, called for territorial autonomy within Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Well, we couldn't say that it called for, but that it rather established it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then, as indicated earlier, it was in December of 1991 that the Republic of Serbian Krajina was declared; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Babic, I'd like to turn now away from the political steps that were taken during that period to some of the factual backdrop to the conflict that emerged in August of 1991, or the more intensified conflict that emerged in August of 1991. Paragraph 16 of your factual basis you indicate, as you have here, that a parallel structure began to emerge from August 1990, comprised of members of the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia, the State Security Service of Serbia, the SDS of Croatia, and policemen in the Serbian municipalities in Croatia, which ultimately Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. answered directly and exclusively to Slobodan Milosevic. You've indicated some of the central figures in the parallel structure, as you have here.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I'm not receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, can you hear the interpretation now?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know when the interpretation stopped, but I had directed your attention and the Court's attention to paragraph 16 of your factual basis in which you describe the emergence of the parallel structure in August of 1990, indicate its membership, and the fact that it ultimately answered directly and exclusively to Mr. Milosevic, and in which you describe some of the central figures of the parallel structure. Now, paragraph 16 goes on to indicate that through the parallel structure Milosevic manufactured incidents which provoked reaction and fear among the Serbs and intensified intervention by the Croatian police. This spiraled up into intolerance, violence, and eventually war. Let me ask you first about the nature of some of the incidents which were conducted by members of the parallel structure. Did those include the blowing up of shops and kiosks owned by Albanians and Croats?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Among others, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you provide the Court with some general indication of the nature of the incidents that were conducted by members of the parallel structure and that provoked reaction and fear among the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Well, I can say that that was a reaction to attempts by myself and some other presidents of municipalities from the area to reach an agreement with the representatives of Croatian government on peaceful resolution to the problems and on -- on finding -- on finding mutual ground, and as a result of that Council of People's Resistance was set up. It was opposed to peaceful solutions, and the parallel structure was responsible for various incidents on the ground; mining of -- blowing up of railways, destroying various stands, kiosks, abuse of citizens, and so on, attempts to knock down power lines. They even managed to disrupt the power supply in order to create greater disturbance. The aim of all this was to provoke the intervention of the JNA into introduce a state of emergency in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the period of -- from 1990 through 1991, were Croatian Serbs provided with arms by members of the parallel structure or others from outside Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Milosevic himself provide arms to the Croatian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: To the Serbs in Croatia, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: From him personally and also from his minister of police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Court the meeting or meetings during which you learned from Mr. Milosevic personally that arms -- that he was providing arms to the Serbs in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: That was in a meeting in March of 1991. The situation was quite tense. I can't remember who exactly proposed that we should go and see Milosevic to ask him what his plan was to protect the Serbs in Croatia. That was what prompted us to ask for the meeting. I went there together with some other people from Krajina. Milosevic told us that he had already purchased 20.000 weapons in Hungary for us. We were surprised. We looked at each other. It was unusual for us to know that Milosevic was buying weapons for us in Hungary when the media reported that it was Croatia that was doing that. Then he invited Radmilo Bogdanovic and Jovica Stanisic -- Radmilo Bogdanovic was a former minister of police, and Radmilo Bogdanovic said that they had already sent 500 weapons to Banija. Later on, sometimes in May, I saw -- I was shown the weapons in a warehouse and was told that the weapons had arrived from the TO warehouse in Serbia and that it had been organised by Mihalj Kertes, a man who was very close to Milosevic and Jovica Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, who showed you the warehouse with the weapons in May of 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Milenko Zelenbaba, chief of police in Knin, an assistant of Martic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of weapons were you shown?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Long-barrelled weapons; rifles and mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Mr. Kertes. Did he have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Braco.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you learned during the course of that conversation with Mr. Zelenbaba that the source of the weapons was TO warehouses or TO defence -- or TO warehouses in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, you've already indicated that during the course of your testimony in the Milosevic case you provided a -- you -- or during your preparation for that you were able to listen to a series of intercepts which are reflected in the declaration that you looked at earlier today. I'd like to turn your attention to one of those.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this -- the transcript of this particular intercept will be found or can be found at page 5 of the attached list of the intercepts. It is a conversation that took place on June 24, 1991, between Radovan Karadzic and Braco.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Babic, let me ask you if you're familiar with that intercept, if you recall it.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remember listening to it. It was also presented in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you a question, then, about a portion of the contents of that. There are references in the intercept to food and supermarket, and if I recall correctly, salt.

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: Yes. Batteries and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Flour, I also see on page 3 of the English translation. Were those the commodities with which Mr. Kertes, to your knowledge -- with which Braco, to your knowledge, was concerned?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I didn't know at the time that he was involved in this. I know that he was exclusively involved in delivering weapons from Serbia and Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you help us then understand the references to flour and salt and supermarkets and so on? Are those references to those items or do they have another meaning in the context of this conversation?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC
utterances.text: I think that this is a superficially coded conversation. It has to do with the delivery of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just in relation to the questioning on the -- the intercepts generally, I would be objecting, and I do object generally to questions which call for speculation on the part of the witness in relation to what other people might be talking about. I would submit it is of fairly limited value to the Trial Chamber. Generally intercepts are there for the Trial Chamber to determine what weight they might be given and what approach might be adopted in relation to their meaning, and asking someone else to comment on other people's conversations when it hasn't actually been established on what precise basis he can determine the meaning on a particular conversation, I think there has to be some caution in that regard, Your Honour, because it can lead to speculation, and I just sound that warning out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, is this a warning that tells you something or --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I fully accept that as a general matter it's the Court's prerogative and responsibility to draw conclusions from the evidence presented to it. On the other hand, I think it's a very common area of inquiry to someone from a certain milieu to identify aspects of conversations which may be better illuminated by someone who operated within that particular context, particularly if it involves some form of coded conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger, you may proceed. It's not inappropriate to ask from a witness if two political leaders are -- or at least, political figures are discussing flour, salt, or perhaps cauliflower or whatever vegetables to try to find out what that might stand for if not for salt, flour, or cauliflower. Ms. Loukas, just for your information, if a witness would say this is about drugs instead of weapons, the Chamber might not follow that witness in establishing that it was about drugs. So the -- it's not pure speculation, but on the other hand, it is some interpretation which will be looked at very cautiously by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wanted to sound that warning at this point because there can be a tendency for there to be tendentious explanations of intercepts, particularly a person who has pleaded guilty and is awaiting sentencing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber is aware of the risks, and the Chamber is aware of the very specific situation in respect to this witness. Mr. Tieger, I don't know what questions you would have liked to have put to the witness during the last two minutes, but they have gone. Therefore, unless there would be one or two questions that you would consider to be necessary at this very moment and they couldn't wait until tomorrow, then we will adjourn until morning, 9.00, in this same courtroom. I've forgotten one thing: Mr. Babic, I should instruct you not to speak with anyone about the testimony you have given or you're still about to give. That also includes members of the Office of the Prosecution, Defence team, friends, visitors, whoever; not to talk about it with anyone. Yes. Then we will adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00.
